reasoning_traces.think:
The ECE estimator suffers from finite-sample bias due to sampling variability. The raw ECE estimate systematically overstates true calibration error, especially in small bins. A debiasing correction is applied by subtracting the expected noise floor derived from Monte Carlo resampling. However, this naive subtraction undercorrects for real gaps. The solution involves adjusting for per-bin variance to better reflect actual calibration error. The dual nature of ECE—both a measure of calibration and a signal of model confidence—requires careful handling of its statistical properties to avoid false positives in eligibility gates. The correction ensures that the gate accurately reflects whether a model is truly calibrated or merely appears so due to noise.
